articles.headline: Bearcat Builds A Home In The Basement, Starts Paying Rent
articles.deck: Hog Tied and Deep Fried craters to 81.28, Davante Adams no shows, and the bench has nothing to say about it
body: Let's be clear about what happened to Bearcat this week, because the box score alone doesn't capture the full scope of the crime scene. Hog Tied and Deep Fried put up 81.28 points, dead last among all 14 teams, got run over by Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs by a cool 31.2, and dropped to 1-6 on a streak that has officially graduated from unlucky to structural: L5. Five losses in a row isn't a slump anymore, it's a lifestyle, and this week it came with a side of rock bottom.

Start with the headliner that wasn't. Davante Adams, a starting wide receiver on this roster, finished the week with zero points on zero projection and an empty stat line, as in nothing happened, as in he may as well have been a folding chair in that WR slot. That is not a bust, that is a hole in the lineup that Bearcat willingly dug and climbed into. Pair that with Mark Andrews quietly no-showing at 5.3 against a 9.18 projection and Denzel Boston turning in 5.7 on a 10.89 expectation, and you get a receiving corps that collectively forgot the sport was being played that day. Brandon McManus chipped in 5 points on a 7.54 projection because even the kicker wanted in on the disappointment.

And here's the part that should really sting: there was no bailout sitting on the bench. Zero bench points. Not one single point left on the table to point at and scream about, no what-if, no cost, no bench call to rage over, because the bench simply produced nothing. Usually a shart game comes with a tragic footnote, a guy on the pine who torched his projection while the starter he replaced face planted. Not here. Bearcat didn't lose this one to bad lineup decisions. He lost it because the whole operation, top to bottom, bench included, just didn't show up. The only player on this roster who played like he had a pulse was Rhamondre Stevenson, who put up 22.5 against an 11.1 projection with a rushing score and a receiving score, and it did not matter even a little bit, because everyone around him was busy filing missing person reports.

Meanwhile Jeff's team on the other side of the carnage got Dak Prescott throwing for 23.28 against a 15.36 projection, Javonte Williams bulldozing his way to 21.5, and Drake London adding 19.6, and Chase Browns with Downs barely had to sweat to hit 112.48. Bearcat's week ranked 14th out of 14, dead last by rank and dead last by points, the full sweep of futility, the kind of week where you check the projections just to confirm you weren't projected to win either, 82.26 projected against 81.28 actual, so even the computer that's supposed to be optimistic about your chances basically shrugged.

This is not new territory for this roster. Week 4 already has Hog Tied and Deep Fried's name stapled to the weekly low at 73.02, and now Week 7 adds 81.28 right next to it, which makes this the second time this man's team has been the single worst scoring outfit in the entire league inside of seven weeks, with two Sharts already on the books before this one even landed. That is not bad luck, that is a track record, a pattern, a brand identity. The Shart used to be a punishment. For Bearcat it is starting to look like a subscription service he forgot to cancel.

So here it is, the full unholy liturgy, bigger than the pitchers, bigger than the hose, bigger than the gas station twelve pack sitting alone in a parking lot. Haul the kiddie pool out of someone's garage, fill it with whatever is left in the house, beer, well liquor, the last sad inch of flat soda, doesn't matter, and lower Bearcat into it like a confirmation ceremony, because two Sharts and a repeat visit to the bottom of the standings by Week 7 demands full baptism, not a sip. He goes under once for 73.02, once for 81.28, and comes up only when the record officially reads worse than 1-6. Chug, bitch.

articles.headline: The Hardware: Week 7 Trophy Case Smells Like Regret And Light Beer
articles.deck: Seven awards, zero dignity. Pull up a folding chair, the commissioner is reading names off an index card again.
body: First up, Manager of the Week, which this round goes to Trip and 50 Shades of Zay for dropping 147.9 points on a league that did not see it coming. Zay Flowers went for 27.7, Luther Burden III chipped in 23.7, Amon-Ra St. Brown added 24.2 and Bucky Irving punched in 24 of his own, and somehow Trip still managed to leave Omar Cooper Jr.'s 22.5 on the bench in favor of Kenneth Walker III's 9.7, a 12.8 point gift to nobody. Winning by that much and still leaving free money on the table is a flex only a man already up 2 games clear of the field can afford.

The Shart goes to Bearcat and Hog tied and deep fried, 81.28 points, beaten by Jeff, now sitting at 1-6 on an L5 streak that has gone from sad to structural. We will circle back to him elsewhere in this paper. Moving on.

Blowout honors go to Trip again, this time for the 65.14 margin he hung on Adam and First Down Syndrome. Derrick Henry no showed at 5.9 against a 16.74 projection, and Adam benched Caleb Williams's 22.12 for Jordan Love's 16.96, a 5.16 point gut punch that did not matter in a loss this ugly but will haunt him anyway.

Squeaker belongs to Jackson, who beat Taylor by a microscopic 0.34, 119.32 to 118.98, while sitting Tony Pollard's 36.5 points in favor of D'Andre Swift's 19, a 17.5 point decision that could have ended the game by halftime had he just trusted his gut.

Lucky Dog is Andrew's, who won with a pedestrian 89.32 while Bryce Young imploded for 5.42 against a 17.92 projection with 2 INT, a mess made worse by benching Aaron Rodgers's 13.08 for the privilege, a 7.66 point own goal that somehow still produced a W.

Heartbreaker goes to Sean, who dropped 125.48, got 28.88 out of Joe Burrow, and still lost to John's 126.42 by 0.94. Bench Rot closes the show and it is Jackson again, 55.90 points stranded on his bench, almost entirely Tony Pollard's fault, in a win decided by a number smaller than a field goal.

articles.headline: Trip Turns First Down Syndrome Into A Group Project He Didn't Have To Do
articles.deck: 147.9 points, a 65.14 margin, and a bench call that almost got away with murder.
body: Trip's 50 Shades of Zay put up 147.9 this week, the best score anybody managed in Week 7, and he did it behind three receivers who all decided to have the same career day at the same time. Zay Flowers went off for 27.7 against an 18.75 projection on an 8 of 11, 137 yard, 1 touchdown line. Luther Burden III was somehow even more absurd, going 4 of 4 for 130 yards and a score, turning in 23.7 points against a 12.53 projection, the single best outlier performance on Trip's own roster this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown chipped in 24.2 on 9 of 11 for 153 yards, just to make sure nobody forgot he exists. That is three different wideouts each beating their number by double digits or close to it in the same lineup, which is not a game plan, that's just getting away with something.

Bucky Irving did his part too, 24 carries for 106 yards and 2 rushing touchdowns, good for 24 points against a 16.43 projection, and Matthew Stafford quietly went 23 of 29 for 195 yards and 3 touchdowns, basically matching his projection to the decimal at 17.5 versus 16.88. This is now 5-2 on the season with a W1 streak, and the margin of victory, 65.14, is the biggest blowout of the week by a mile.

Here's the part where we undercut him a little. Kenneth Walker III started in the flex and gave Trip 9.7 points against a 19.38 projection, a near double digit miss, while Omar Cooper Jr. sat on the bench and dropped 22.5. That is a 12.8 point gift Trip handed himself and didn't even need, because the man he beat, Adam's First Down Syndrome, was busy setting itself on fire on the other side of the field. Derrick Henry gave Adam 5.9 points on a 16.74 projection, Sam LaPorta turned 13.49 projected points into 2.8 actual ones, and the Houston Texans defense posted a zero against an 8.59 projection. Adam's team ranked 13th in scoring this week. Trip's ranked 1st. That is not a competitive football game, that is a mugging.

Zoom out and 147.9 is a great week, but it is not even the best number in the book this year. Romo911 dropped 174.86 back in Week 5, Jackson's squad opened the year with 169.86, and Cook'd put up 154.78 in Week 4. So Trip gets the trophy, the bragging rights, and a Walker-sized reminder that he left 33 points on his own bench while doing it. Still 5-2 beats the alternative. Go enjoy the win, Trip, and maybe bench Kenneth Walker next time before the stat sheet does it for you.

articles.headline: Jackson Leaves 55.9 on the Bench and Still Survives by 0.34
articles.deck: Taylor's Victorious Secrets throw everything at Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy and lose by less than the cost of a Josef Zyn can
body: Jackson improved to 6-1 and stretched his win streak to W2 the hard way, needing every one of his 119.32 points to hold off Taylor's 118.98 in a margin so thin it earned the Squeaker trophy outright. Taylor, now 1-6 and riding an L2 skid, did everything a desperate team is supposed to do. He just did it 0.34 points short.

Taylor's case for the upset starts with Bo Nix going off for 26.18 points on 15 of 29 for 222 yards with a touchdown through the air and another on the ground, and Makai Lemon turning a modest 8.92 projection into 19.7 real points on 7 of 8 receiving for 67 yards and a score. That is the kind of week where you expect to win. Instead Taylor's own bench decision bit him too, sitting the Cincinnati Bengals defense, who put up 8 points, in favor of the Dallas Cowboys, who managed 4. That is points walked away from, in a game decided by 0.34.

Jackson's side of the ledger is no cleaner. Ashton Jeanty was the engine, posting 21.6 points on 8 catches for 61 yards and a touchdown despite only 8 carries, and Puka Nacua chipped in 21.8 on a near-projection week. But Tyler Shough was pedestrian at 13.82, and Christian Watson face planted against a 17.99 projection, catching 5 of 8 for a quiet 57 yards and only 10.7 points. This was not a vintage lineup. It was a lineup that happened to score 0.34 more than the other guy.

And then there is the call that should have blown this game up entirely. Jackson benched Tony Pollard, who went for 36.5 points, in favor of D'Andre Swift, who returned 19 in the FLEX spot. That is a 17.5 point gap, the single costliest bench decision of the week anywhere in the league, and it left Jackson sitting on 55.9 bench points overall, enough to claim the Bench Rot trophy for the week outright. Most managers who leave that kind of production on their own bench lose. Jackson did not. He just barely, miraculously, did not.

Zoom out and this was not even the only nail biter on the slate. Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 beat Matt's Shough Her Gently by 0.52 after Matt sat Cam Skattebo's 19.1 points for A.J. Brown's 7.8, an 11.3 point gift that nearly cost him anyway. John's BedBathNBIJAN22 edged Sean's Burrowed Alive by 0.94 after benching Blake Corum's 17.1 for Woody Marks' 9.1. Both of those games were decided by less than a point, and both winners left better players on their own bench. But neither came close to Jackson's bench math, and neither finished tighter than 0.34. Taylor walks away with the best loss of his season and nothing to show for it. Jackson walks away 6-1, still owning the top seed, and should probably stop benching 36.5 point games before his luck runs out for good.

articles.headline: Matt And Taylor Both Hand Their Own Wins Away In Week 7
articles.deck: A night built entirely on fractions of a point, bad bench buttons, and Trip going nuclear while everyone else fought over inches.
body: Fourteen teams took the field in Week 7 and somehow three different games came down to less than a single point. Two separate dudes benched the actual winning lineup. Trip dropped 147.9 and lapped the field by a number so big it should have its own zip code. Welcome to the dumbest, tightest week of the year.

Ben's Jackson Off ran past Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher 101.3 to 88.9, and the whole thing turned on Josh Jacobs quietly going for 20.1 against an 11.95 projection while Patrick Mahomes imploded for Josef, throwing a pick and managing only 6 points against a 15.64 number. Ben still benched Marvin Harrison Jr.'s 7.6 for Xavier Worthy's 4.1, a 3.5 point gift to nobody, but the margin covered the sin.

Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 survived Matt's Shough Her Gently 89.32 to 88.8, a margin of 0.52, and Matt is the reason he lost. He benched Cam Skattebo's 19.1 in favor of A.J. Brown's 7.8, an 11.3 point gap that alone would have flipped this game, capping a brutal L5 skid at 1-6. Andrew, meanwhile, got bailed out by Tee Higgins going off for 26.8 against a 15.04 projection, because his own bench calls, Aaron Rodgers over Bryce Young and Rome Odunze over Jalen Coker, cost him 7.66 and 9 points respectively.

Trip's 50 Shades of Zay demolished Adam's First Down Syndrome 147.9 to 82.76, a 65.14 point massacre, with Zay Flowers going for 27.7 and Luther Burden III adding 23.7 against a 12.53 number. Adam's Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 31.3 in a losing effort, and Adam somehow still benched Caleb Williams' 22.12 for Jordan Love's 16.96, because why not add insult to the injury.

Sean's Burrowed Alive lost to John's BedBathNBIJAN22 126.42 to 125.48, a margin of 0.94, and this one is entirely on Sean. He sat Ryan Flournoy's 11 points for Keenan Allen's 6.1, a 4.9 point decision that would have won the game outright. Joe Burrow went for 28.88 for Sean, but the Eagles defense cratered for negative 7 against a 5.95 projection, and John's Trey McBride answered with 27.1 against a 15.43 number to seal it.

The actual Squeaker of the week belonged to Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, who edged Taylor's Victorious Secrets 119.32 to 118.98, a margin of 0.34. Taylor started the Cowboys defense over the Bengals defense, a 4 point call that would have flipped this result by itself, while Jackson left 36.5 points of Tony Pollard on his own bench, the single biggest bench rot number of the season, and still somehow walked away with the win.

Jack's Cook'd kept rolling, a sixth straight win, beating Aaron's Romo911 108.02 to 88.34. Quinshon Judkins exploded for 23.4 against an 11.18 projection and Colston Loveland added 19.9 against a 9.82 number, while Aaron's Nico Collins no-showed for 2.6 against a 17.1 projection and Justin Jefferson managed only 8.4 against 16.91. Drake Maye's 27.44 was not nearly enough cover.

Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs ran over Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried 112.48 to 81.28, a 31.2 point blowout that extends Bearcat's L5 and drops him to 1-6 with the Shart trophy to show for it. Dak Prescott threw for 23.28 against a 15.36 projection for Jeff, even after he benched Devaughn Vele's 16.4 in favor of Garrett Wilson's 4.6, an 11.8 point donation that didn't end up mattering. Rhamondre Stevenson's 22.5 was the lone bright spot for Bearcat in a game that was never close.

articles.headline: Waiver Wire Report Week 7 Where The Real Studs Live On Benches
articles.deck: The adds and afterthoughts outscored the stars, and a couple of guys in the league found that out the hard way
body: Nobody on this app understands roster construction like the guys who refuse to use their best players. Matt's Shough Her Gently, record 1-6, still lost by 0.52 to Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69, which is its own tragedy, but buried in that box score is Tre Tucker going for 21.3 against a projection of 9.06. That is a league winning flex play sitting on a losing roster, and Matt still found a way to lose by less than a point because apparently stacking receivers correctly is the one thing this group cannot do.

Luther Burden III put up 23.7 for Trip's 50 Shades of Zay in a week where the whole roster went supernova anyway, 147.9 points, the best score in the league. Burden projected for 12.53. That is not a floor play anymore, that is a bellcow in a rookie's body, and 50 Shades of Zay is riding him at 5-2 straight into the playoff picture at 92.3 percent to make it.

John's BedBathNBIJAN22, sitting at 3-4, got 23.2 out of KC Concepcion Jr. against a 9.72 projection and 26.1 out of Jameson Williams against 12.53, which is how you win by 0.94 over Sean's Burrowed Alive despite Brock Purdy throwing 2 interceptions. That is a receiving corps getting good at exactly the right moment.

Meanwhile the real crime scenes. Jackson benched Tony Pollard, who went for 36.5, in favor of D'Andre Swift's 19, and still won by 0.34, which should be illegal. Adam benched Caleb Williams and his 22.12 for Jordan Love's 16.96 and lost by 65.14, which means the bench points never even mattered, the whole operation was broken. Bearcat got 22.5 off Rhamondre Stevenson and still posted 81.28 for the week's lowest score. Add the right guy. Start him too.

articles.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Torches Seattle, Adam Torches His Own Season
articles.deck: Six monster games littered the box scores this week and somehow four of the guys who had them still lost. Football is cruel. Fantasy football is crueler.
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba went 9/12 for 150 yards and a touchdown, tacked on two carries for 13 more, and finished with 31.3 points against a 24.3 projection, the single highest number anybody put up all week. Adam started him. Adam still lost 82.76 to 147.9 in the Week 7 wood chipper, because that's what happens when your QB1 benches Caleb Williams for Jordan Love and the rest of the roster no-shows behind him. JSN posted the best line in the league and First Down Syndrome dropped to 3-4 anyway.

Joe Burrow threw for 292 yards and 4 touchdowns, good for 28.88 points on a 19.26 projection, and Sean still lost. Burrowed Alive fell to BedBathNBIJAN22 126.42 to 125.48, officially this week's Heartbreaker, the highest score to lose a game. Burrow did everything. The Philadelphia Eagles defense did the opposite, bleeding 38 points allowed for a minus-7.

Zay Flowers actually got to matter. His 137 yards and a score were worth 27.7 points on an 18.75 projection, part of the onslaught that buried First Down Syndrome by 65.14, the week's Blowout. Trip didn't need the heroics but got them anyway, which feels unfair to everybody else in this paragraph.

Drake Maye threw for 321 yards and ran one in himself for 27.44 points, miles past his 20.4 projection, and Aaron's Romo911 still got run over by Cook'd, 88.34 to 108.02. Trey McBride caught 10 of 13 targets for 111 yards and a score, 27.1 points against a 15.43 projection, and that was the difference in John's 0.94 win over Sean. Tee Higgins went for 148 yards and a touchdown, 26.8 points on a 15.04 projection, in a game Andrew's Bibi's Ballers won with only 89.32, officially the week's Lucky Dog. And on the bench, Tony Pollard dropped 36.5 points for Jackson, who didn't start him, which is its own kind of big performance nobody got to cash in on.

articles.headline: Power Rankings Week 7: Trip Rockets Up While Josef Free Falls
articles.deck: Fourteen teams, one Shart, and a bench full of regret. Here's who actually deserves your respect this week.
body: Nobody moved at the top because nobody needed to. The rest of the league spent Week 7 benching their best players and losing by nothing, while these two just kept winning.

1. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson, 6-1, W2): Jackson won the Squeaker of the Week by 0.34 over Taylor and still somehow left 55.90 points on his bench, including Tony Pollard's 36.5 rotting there while D'Andre Swift's 19 started instead. That is a 17.5 point gift to himself that he didn't even need, which is the most 1-seed thing imaginable.

2. Cook'd (Jack, 6-1, W6): Six straight wins and Jack barely sweated this one, riding Quinshon Judkins' 23.4 and Colston Loveland's 19.9 to a 19.68 point beatdown of Aaron. The scary part is that score only ranked 7th across the league this week. He's winning while mediocre.

3. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip, 5-2, W1): Trip dropped 147.9 on the league, the Manager of the Week and the Blowout trophy in the same breath, powered by Zay Flowers' 27.7 and Luther Burden's absurd 23.7. He even left Omar Cooper Jr.'s 22.5 on the bench and still won by 65.14. Absolute war crime.

4. Jackson Off (Ben, 5-2, W3): Ben won by 12.4 despite posting the 8th best score of the week, because Josh Jacobs went off for 20.1 against a projection of 11.95. He also benched Marvin Harrison Jr.'s 7.6 for Xavier Worthy's 4.1, a 3.5 point unforced error that didn't end up mattering, this time.

5. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff, 5-2, W1): Jeff crushed Bearcat by 31.2 thanks to Dak Prescott's 23.28, but Garrett Wilson no showed with 4.6 against a 16.76 projection while Devaughn Vele sat there with 16.4 unused. An 11.8 point gift that still didn't cost him a thing against this week's opponent.

6. Romo911 (Aaron, 4-3, L1): Drake Maye threw for 27.44 and it still wasn't enough, because Nico Collins turned a 17.1 projection into 2.6 actual points, a disappearing act that doomed him in a loss to Cook'd. Aaron's two sharts this season are starting to feel like a personality trait.

7. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John, 3-4, W1): John won by 0.94 with Trey McBride going nuclear for 27.1 and Jameson Williams adding 26.1, but he also benched Blake Corum's 17.1 for Woody Marks' 9.1. Cost him 8 points in a game decided by less than one. He got away with it, barely.

8. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew, 3-4, W1): The Lucky Dog trophy goes to Andrew, who won with just 89.32 points while benching Aaron Rodgers' 13.08 for Bryce Young's 5.42 and Rome Odunze's 10.9 for Jalen Coker's 1.9. Tee Higgins bailed him out with 26.8, because somebody had to.

9. First Down Syndrome (Adam, 3-4, L1): Jaxon Smith-Njigba went off for 31.3, the single best performance in the league this week, and Adam still lost by 65.14 because literally everyone else on his roster no showed. Caleb Williams' 22.12 sat on his bench behind Jordan Love's 16.96. Rough.

10. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef, 4-3, L1): Biggest faller in the rankings, and Patrick Mahomes is the reason why, throwing for 165 yards and an interception on his way to 6 points against a 15.64 projection. Emeka Egbuka scored a literal zero. Josef needed a bounce back and got a brick.

11. Burrowed Alive (Sean, 2-5, L1): Sean's Heartbreaker trophy says it all, 125.48 points and a loss, with Joe Burrow throwing for 292 and 4 touchdowns for 28.88. The Philadelphia Eagles defense gave back negative 7 points after allowing 38. That's not a typo, that's a crime scene.

12. Victorious Secrets (Taylor, 1-6, L2): Bo Nix put up 26.18 and Makai Lemon added 19.7, and Taylor still lost the Squeaker by 0.34 after benching the Bengals defense's 8 points for the Cowboys' 4. That 4 point decision was bigger than the entire margin. Painful math nobody asked him to do.

13. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat, 1-6, L5): The Shart belongs to Bearcat again, 81.28 points and a fifth straight loss, saved only slightly by Rhamondre Stevenson's 22.5 while Davante Adams contributed a flat zero. Two shart trophies on the season now. A chug is owed.

14. Shough Her Gently (Matt, 1-6, L5): Matt lost by 0.52 after benching Cam Skattebo's 19.1 for A.J. Brown's 7.8, an 11.3 point decision in a game that came down to half a point. Five straight losses and he's doing it to himself at this point.

articles.headline: The Trade Desk Is Closed, So Enjoy These Self Inflicted Gunshot Wounds Instead
articles.deck: Zero trades got done in Week 7. Several men still managed to trade a win for a loss using only their own bench.
body: Let the record show the Squirtnite FFL trade desk did not do a single lick of business this week. Not one deal. Not a throwaway kicker swap, not a desperation flex shuffle, nothing. The phones just sat there ringing into the void while fourteen grown men decided the real action was in benching their own good players instead, which is somehow worse and infinitely funnier, so that is the column you get.

Start with Matt, Shough Her Gently, who lost to Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 by 0.52 after sitting Cam Skattebo and his 19.1 points in favor of A.J. Brown's 7.8. That is an 11.3 point unforced error in a game decided by less than one point. Grade on that trade with himself: F, with the body still warm.

Andrew somehow survived his own sins and still deserves a write up. He benched Aaron Rodgers and his 13.08 for Bryce Young's 5.42, then benched Rome Odunze's 10.9 for Jalen Coker's 1.9, torching 7.66 and 9 points respectively, and still won with 89.32, officially the Lucky Dog of the week. Grade: D minus, you do not get style points for surviving a car crash you caused yourself.

Adam of First Down Syndrome benched Caleb Williams and his 22.12 for Jordan Love's 16.96 in a game he lost by 65.14 to Trip's 50 Shades of Zay. That swap alone was not the reason for the beatdown, but a 5.16 point gift on top of a loss that lopsided is just mean to himself. Grade: F.

And Jackson, Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, won his game by the tightest of margins at 0.34 over Taylor while sitting Tony Pollard's 36.5 for D'Andre Swift's 19, an 17.5 point haircut that also earned him the league lead in Bench Rot at 55.90 unused points. Winning covers a multitude of sins. Grade: incomplete, pending a cardiologist's note.

articles.headline: Next Up Trip Crashes Jackson's Party While Matt Hosts The Shart Bowl
articles.deck: The league's two best teams collide, Cook'd rolls into the league's saddest building, and Shough Her Gently might set a new low before the ink even dries.
body: The marquee matchup next week sends Trip's 50 Shades of Zay, fresh off dropping 147.9 and riding a W1, into Jackson's building at Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, who sits 6-1 on a W2 and is the top seed in the league. Trip is 5-2 and climbing power rankings behind Zay Flowers going off for 27.7, so this is basically a play-in game for whoever isn't already measuring for a playoff bye.

Elsewhere Jack's Cook'd machine, winners of six straight and sitting 6-1, rolls into Bearcat's house. Bearcat is 1-6, on an L5, and is still holding the Shart trophy from this week's 81.28 face plant. There is no version of this where Hog Tied and Deep Fried is favored, there is only the question of how bad it gets.

Now for the Shart Bowl. Matt's Shough Her Gently owns the league's lowest points for total at 606.5, is 1-6, and is deep into an L5 that shows no signs of stopping. He draws Ben's Jackson Off, a 5-2 squad riding a W3 that just dropped a dub on the Zyn-bo Squisher. A historically punchless offense facing a team that is actually playing good defense and good ball is exactly the recipe for next week's lowest score, and Matt is the betting favorite to collect his second shart related reputation hit of the season.

The bubble gets a borderline sibling rivalry too, as Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 at 3-4 and a W1 host John's BedBathNBIJAN22, also 3-4 and also on a W1, both clawing for the same playoff spot off last week's nail biters. Meanwhile Aaron's Romo911, 4-3 and nursing an L1 after Nico Collins no showed for 2.6, visits Sean's Burrowed Alive, also 2-5 and L1 despite Sean dropping 125.48 and still losing. And Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, 5-2 and W1, head into Taylor's building, where Victorious Secrets sits 1-6 on an L2 and still hunting for anything resembling momentum.

body: No stat corrections changed a published result this week.
